POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on H.R. 6398, the Chair put the question on motion to recommit, and by voice vote, announced that the noes had prevailed. Mrs. Grijalva demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
The previous question on the motion to recommit was ordered pursuant to clause 2(b) of rule XIX.
Mrs. Grijalva moved to recommit to the Committee on Energy and Commerce. (text: CR H2912-2913)
The previous question was ordered pursuant to the rule.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies proposing regulations and construction projects, as well as the Environmental Protection Agency.
dimensions.evidence: review by the Environmental Protection Agency of proposed legislation

dimensions.assessment: Removes a procedural review step for certain federal projects and regulations, altering administrative workflows.
dimensions.evidence: removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) review and comment

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply any specific fiscal or economic effects.
Amends Section 309 of the Clean Air Act to narrow the scope of mandatory EPA project and regulation reviews.
dimensions.evidence: Section 309 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7609) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change affecting all future applicable federal projects and proposed regulations nationwide.

missing_information: Estimates of time or cost savings resulting from the removal of the EPA review requirement.
importance_detail.rationale: Removes a specific EPA review and comment requirement under the Clean Air Act for actions already reviewed under NEPA and proposed federal regulations, streamlining administrative processes for federal projects.

Res. 1156) expressing support for tax policies that support working families.
